content.comment_body: Hello, I'm new to this forum. I searched previous posts but couldn't find an answer. I want to control certain parts of my software (for testing) using the onboard arrow keys of [product_name]. Simulating the program works fine, but once it's transferred to the PLC, the keys don't respond. Is there a setting to enable key control during program execution?
Hi, Remember, you need to press both the Esc and cursor keys in order to use the cursor keys on [product_name] hardware. For more details, check [url]. Regards, [user_name]

I experienced this issue too, [user_name]. Pressing ESC does help somewhat, but I ended up redesigning my system so I didn't need the cursor keys. [company_name] advises that using their keypad should work flawlessly, though I haven't tested it. They also claim these problems are resolved in [version_no], but I haven't tried that either. Good luck!

It works with ESC plus Cursor Key, but you need to act quickly. Holding ESC too long won't work. In [version_no], you can use [product_name] operator devices and function keys, which are much more comfortable and look better. Wishing you more success!
Thank you for your help. This forum is quick and helpful. I tried ESC plus Arrow Key but it puts me in a menu that shows I/O status. What could I be doing wrong?

You just need to do it quickly—press them at the same time, briefly. You should see a quick flash on the arrow display. I tested this yesterday in [product_name] with [article_no] installed at my weekend house and it worked.

- Go to the screen for cursor key usage (move left once from date/time) as explained in the manual, then you can use them. - Alternatively, create a message text; when a message is shown, the keys become usable right away. From other positions in the [product_name] menu, pressing ESC (and then cursor key) may cause different responses.

analysis.insight_summary: Users encounter difficulties when trying to use onboard arrow keys for process control directly via [product_name] hardware while the program is running. Keypress control is possible but requires pressing the ESC and arrow keys simultaneously, quickly, and with precise timing, which users do not find straightforward. Behavior varies depending on [version_no], with reports of better usability and operator devices in newer versions.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to control program steps directly on the [product_name] device using arrow keys during operation. They want an intuitive, reliable, and simple key-based control method without having to perform complex or time-sensitive key combinations.
